title: Is it possible to make Streamlit interactive plot as fast as Plotly?
body:
### Problem

[![Open in Streamlit Cloud](https://static.streamlit.io/badges/streamlit_badge_black_white.svg)](https://issues.streamlitapp.com/?issue=gh-6978)

I am trying to create a responsive plot in Streamlit that responds to a slider bar, but it is extremely slow.
```
import numpy as np
import plotly.graph_objects as go
import streamlit as st


if st.session_state.get('fig') is None:
    st.session_state['freq'] = np.arange(0.0, 5.1, 0.1).round(2)    
    f = st.session_state['freq'][2]
    st.session_state['fig'] = go.Figure()
    st.session_state['fig'].add_trace(
        go.Scatter(
            name=str(f),
            x=np.arange(0, 10.01, 0.01),
            y=np.sin(f* np.arange(0, 10.01, 0.01))))
    
def sldier_callback():
    f = st.session_state['slider_freq']
    x = st.session_state['fig'].data[0].x
    st.session_state['fig'].data[0].y = np.sin(f*x)
    st.session_state['fig'].data[0].name = str(f)


f = st.select_slider(
    label='Frequency', 
    options=st.session_state['freq'],
    value=2,
    on_change=sldier_callback,
    key='slider_freq'
)

st.plotly_chart(st.session_state['fig'])
```
![image](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/assets/15989924/de4641d3-ee8b-44f3-9893-81f58d371e17)

### Solution

The [Plotly chart](https://plotly.com/python/sliders/), on the other hand, is much more responsive to the slider bar. It creates and hides the figures at the beginning and then unhides the correct figure when you move the slider bar.
```
import plotly.graph_objects as go
import numpy as np


fig = go.Figure()
for step in np.arange(0, 5, 0.1):
    fig.add_trace(
        go.Scatter(
            visible=False,
            name="f = " + str(step),
            x=np.arange(0, 10, 0.01),
            y=np.sin(step * np.arange(0, 10, 0.01))))

fig.data[10].visible = True

# Create and add slider
steps = []
for i in range(len(fig.data)):
    step = dict(
        method="update",
        args=[              
            {"visible": [False] * len(fig.data)},
            {"title": "Slider switched to step: " + str(i)}],  
    )
    step["args"][0]["visible"][i] = True
    steps.append(step)

sliders = [dict(
    active=10,
    currentvalue={"prefix": "Frequency: "},
    pad={"t": 50},
    steps=steps
)]

fig.update_layout(
    sliders=sliders
)

fig.show()
```

![image](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/assets/15989924/b1c3b597-9a86-403f-8e6b-8ce9bfe3e0dc)


### Additional context

I tried to do the same in Streamlit with the following code, but it is still very slow. Does anyone know how to speed it up in Streamlit? Thanks!

```
import streamlit as st
import numpy as np
import plotly.graph_objects as go


if st.session_state.get('fig') is None:
    st.session_state['freq'] = np.arange(0.0, 5.01, 0.1).round(2)
    st.session_state['fig'] = go.Figure()
    for f in st.session_state['freq']:
        st.session_state['fig'].add_trace(
            go.Scatter(
                visible=False,
                name=str(f),
                x=np.arange(0, 10.01, 0.01),
                y=np.sin(f*np.arange(0, 10.01, 0.01))))
    
    st.session_state['selected'] = 0
    st.session_state['fig'].data[0].visible = True


def sldier_callback():
    i = st.session_state['selected']
    st.session_state['fig'].data[i].visible = False
    freq = st.session_state['slider_freq']
    i = np.where(st.session_state['freq']==freq)[0][0]
    st.session_state['fig'].data[i].visible = True
    st.session_state['selected'] = i


f = st.select_slider(
    label='freq', 
    options=st.session_state['freq'],
    value=2,
    on_change=sldier_callback,
    key='slider_freq'
)

st.plotly_chart(st.session_state['fig'])
```

comments.body:
[USER] Thanks for the enhancement request. I was able to reproduce this [here](https://issues.streamlitapp.com/?issue=gh-6978). Two important pieces of information on this: 
1. using `st.slider` will always be slower than the approach that directly combines it with a plotly slider since the `st.slider` approach requires a roundtrip from frontend -> backend -> frontend, while the Plotly slider only works on the frontend. 
2. You can just use the plotly slider also on a Streamlit frontend with the same speed, e.g.:

```python
import streamlit as st
import plotly.graph_objects as go
import numpy as np


fig = go.Figure()
for step in np.arange(0, 5, 0.1):
    fig.add_trace(
        go.Scatter(
            visible=False,
            name="f = " + str(step),
            x=np.arange(0, 10, 0.01),
            y=np.sin(step * np.arange(0, 10, 0.01))))

fig.data[10].visible = True

# Create and add slider
steps = []
for i in range(len(fig.data)):
    step = dict(
        method="update",
        args=[              
            {"visible": [False] * len(fig.data)},
            {"title": "Slider switched to step: " + str(i)}],  
    )
    step["args"][0]["visible"][i] = True
    steps.append(step)

sliders = [dict(
    active=10,
    currentvalue={"prefix": "Frequency: "},
    pad={"t": 50},
    steps=steps
)]

fig.update_layout(
    sliders=sliders
)

st.plotly_chart(fig)
```

[USER], thanks for your suggestion. I will use your technique for the single slider bar application. But if I need more than one slider bar to control my chart, then Plotly won't work. I hope Streamlit can address this issue in the future.

Closing this since we provide `st.fragment` that allows to group widgets with charts or other elements to provide very fast interactions between those. This will still not be as fast as native plotly widgets since it still requires a roundtrip to our server.
